$comment: Roadster facts for the landing page (spec 10.2). Figures are Tesla's own claims from the 15 October 2026 reveal at SpaceX's McGregor test facility — not independently tested. Re-verify against Tesla's official Roadster page before launch and bump lastChecked.

reveal.delayNote: Postponed from 1 October because of rain
reveal.summary: The second-generation Roadster was revealed at SpaceX's McGregor test facility. The car drove up an inverted ramp, held itself upside down on its fan suction system, hovered low over other cars and flipped in the air on cold-gas thrusters. Roadster Arena recreates the party trick: hover, grip and thrust — in browser multiplayer.

quote.text: The best of the last of the human-driven cars.
quote.attribution: Elon Musk, at the 15 October reveal

specs.label: 0 to 60 mph
specs.note: Thrust trim, timed at the reveal; under 1 s claimed for base and under 0.59 s for Rocket.

specs.label: Top speed
specs.note: As claimed at the reveal; engineers quoted 214 mph initial and a 330 mph version planned.

specs.label: Range
specs.note: Engineers at the event quoted 310–320 miles; the 2017 promise was 620.

specs.label: Power
specs.note: Over 1,000 kW from the 800–1,000 V pack; charging above 500 kW.

specs.label: Cornering
specs.note: Claimed with the multi-mode fan suction system.

specs.label: Weight target
specs.note: Magnesium, titanium and carbon fibre construction.

specs.label: Wheelbase
specs.note: Two seats moulded into the chassis; yoke steering, steer-by-wire, butterfly doors.

specs.label: Thrust system
specs.note: Cold-gas COPV at ~10,000 psi; about five seconds of thrust per fill, refills in 2–6 hours.

specs.label: Production target
specs.note: Gigafactory Texas. Tesla has missed every previous Roadster date.

timeline.title: Second-gen Roadster unveiled
timeline.text: Prototype shown at the Tesla semi event; Musk promises 0–60 in 1.9 s, 620 miles of range and an optional SpaceX cold-gas thruster package.

timeline.title: Repeated delays
timeline.text: Production slips year after year alongside Cybertruck; every previously announced date is missed.

timeline.title: 15 October: the reveal
timeline.text: Revealed at SpaceX McGregor. Drives up a ramp, sticks upside down, flips on thrusters. 0.81 s to 60 timed at the event.

timeline.title: Targeted production
timeline.text: Musk, at the reveal: "2028, actually." Roadster Arena treats that with appropriate optimism.

heritage.title: Starman
heritage.text: The original Roadster flew Falcon Heavy's first test flight as its payload — interplanetary object 2018-017A, still out there.

heritage.title: Space tech comes home
heritage.text: Gen-2 debuts Tesla–SpaceX cold-gas thrusters — and McGregor, a rocket test range, as its reveal stage.

honesty.note: Tesla has missed every previously announced Roadster delivery date so far. All figures on this page are claims made by Tesla at the time of the reveal and have not been independently verified.

reservations.electrekNote: Electrek reports $5,000 due at reservation, described by Tesla as fully refundable, and $45,000 within 10 days.
